findings.issue: reverse() never checks that the locked SALE belongs to the event's orderId. A forged or buggy RETURN_REFUNDED that pairs order X with a returnShipmentId from order Y reverses Y's SALE. The REFUND_REVERSAL and COMMISSION_REVERSAL rows are then written with order_id = X, so order_id on ledger rows stops being consistent. The cap still holds, so this does not create money; it puts the reversal on the wrong order. Design 2.1 step 2 selects order_id, but the code drops it.
findings.fix: Select order_id in the FOR UPDATE query. If it differs from the event's orderId, post nothing and write an UNMATCHED_REVERSAL (or a new kind) row, or throw IllegalArgumentException so the event goes to the DLT. Write the SALE's order_id on the reversal rows.

findings.issue: The comment and ADR claim reversal 'cannot deadlock' with a payout run. That holds only when one SALE row is locked. reverseRefund(order, null|list) locks several SALE rows one after another in one transaction (in shipment_id order). The payout run locks every eligible row with one unordered SELECT ... FOR UPDATE. A multi-shipment reverseRefund and a payout run can therefore deadlock. Postgres would abort one of them, so nothing is corrupted. There is no event caller in part A, but part B is meant to use this method.
findings.fix: Either have part B call reverse once per shipment, each in its own transaction, or add ORDER BY id to the payout run's FOR UPDATE and lock all of the order's SALE rows in one ordered statement. Correct the comment and ADR 0012 to say the guarantee is single-shipment only, and record this on the condition (d) debt line.

findings.issue: The LEDGER ALERT log prints returnId and returnShipmentId exactly as they arrive in the payload, before they are parsed as UUIDs, so a crafted value with CR/LF can forge log lines. orderId is safe because it was already parsed at line 90. No PII is logged: only UUIDs and an amount, and the exception message carries only orderId.
findings.fix: Log only whether each field is present (for example returnId present=true/false), or strip control characters and cap the length before logging.

findings.issue: track() trusts sellerId and amount from any event. At equal or higher rank the amount is overwritten, and the first insert fixes seller_id. That is fine while the register only feeds reports. But the planned T8 repair books recordDelivered from the register amount, and OrderFeignClient.shipment re-confirms only status and seller, not amount. Separately, track() runs before the postings for the whole event, so one malformed part (for example a bad sellerId UUID) now sends the whole event to the DLT before any part is posted. Before, the earlier parts were posted first. The DLT replay recovers this.
findings.fix: In T8, do not book a repair from an unconfirmed register amount (require an authoritative amount or an admin-entered one, and audit it). Optionally validate every part before track() so the failure mode is explicit.

findings.issue: The sums query (WHERE shipment_id = :s, all types, both keys) has no index that covers rows with return_id set. The only shipment index is the partial ux_ledger_shipment_type WHERE return_id IS NULL. As ledger_entries grows, each reversal can scan the table while holding the SALE row lock, which lengthens lock waits and payout contention.
findings.fix: Add a plain index on ledger_entries(shipment_id) in V3, or in V4 if V3 has already been applied anywhere.

findings.issue: This checkpoint (T1-T5) adds the reconcile config and starts writing UNMATCHED_REVERSAL rows, but it has no LedgerReconciler and no repair path. A RETURN_REFUNDED that arrives before DELIVERED is recorded and then never applied, so the seller stays overpaid until T7/T8 land. This is not a regression (the old code skipped it with a warn), but it must not ship as is.
findings.fix: Do not release part A until T7/T8 are merged and reviewed. Gate the push on the final SHA review.

summary: No blocker or major findings on the money path at c316236 (source read from the detached F-20261119-13A worktree). The cap holds. Every reversal, per-return or legacy, takes the SALE row lock with FOR UPDATE. The replay check and the remainder (summed over both keys) are read under that lock, and under READ COMMITTED those reads see whatever a competing reversal committed. So SALE cannot be reversed past its amount, whether by replay, by per-return and legacy reversals combined in either order, or concurrently. A negative or zero returnItemsValue posts nothing (amt <= 0). An oversized one is capped with a WARN. The sellerId and currency come from the booked SALE, never from the event. FEE_REVERSAL copies the booked FEE row (same amount and currency) on the per-shipment partial unique key with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and only on the completing reversal, so it is written at most once. Commission uses the booked C/S ratio, is capped at what is left, and has no divide-by-zero path. Reversals only insert, so rows with payout_id set are never edited. A single-shipment reversal holds one lock and then only inserts, so it cannot deadlock with a payout run. The multi-shipment reverseRefund can deadlock, but it has no caller yet (minor, for part B). The malformed-event path throws IllegalArgumentException, which DlqErrorHandlers does not retry. The ALERT log carries only IDs and an amount, so no PII, but two of those fields are logged raw (minor log-forging risk). V3 is safe. The plain DROP of the CHECK fails loudly on a wrong name. The re-added CHECK only widens the allowed types. The seed cannot collide on the primary key because SALE is unique per shipment where return_id IS NULL and shipment_id is NOT NULL. The new tables are additive. The libs/common-web additions (spring-kafka, jackson-databind) are test-scope only, with versions from the catalog/BOM, and add no new vendor. This checkpoint changes no endpoints, so the auth checks on the planned admin endpoints (T8) still need review on the final SHA. Main follow-ups: check the SALE's order_id against the event, make the deadlock claim accurate for part B, and do not let T8 repair trust the register amount.
